title: retraction/v1 — in-toto predicate body for retracting a prior attestation
description:
Predicate body of an in-toto Statement v1 whose predicateType is https://evals.intentsolutions.io/retraction/v1. A retraction does NOT delete the original attestation (it remains in the transparency log); it is an APPEND-ONLY signed record stating that the platform has chosen not to surface a prior subject and why. The dashboard renders a tombstone at the deep link per the retraction-protocol binding. The `reason_class` enum is CLOSED — open-text reasons are rejected by the schema (GC refusal binding). This schema validates ONLY the predicate body — the enclosing in-toto Statement envelope (_type, subject, predicateType) is validated separately. Each row independently verifiable; NO top-level bundle signature per Blueprint B § 7 line 754.

ADDITIVE in kernel v0.2.0: net-new predicate URI; no v0.1 contract changes. Per § 7.2 backward-compat, adding a predicate URI is allowed; the body normative spec lands here. Runs in sigstore_staging until production-Rekor unlock per DR-010 Q3.

retracted_subject.description: Reference to the subject being retracted — the prior EvidenceBundle / in-toto Statement. At least one of bundle_id or storage_key MUST be present so the retraction is resolvable to a concrete artifact.

bundle_id.description: UUIDv7 of the EvidenceBundle being retracted (FK → EvidenceBundle.id).

storage_key.description: Content-addressed object-storage key of the retracted bundle payload (EvidenceBundle.storage_key).

content_hash.description: sha256-prefixed digest of the retracted artifact, pinning exactly which content is retracted even if a storage backend re-keys.

reason_class.description: CLOSED-SET reason class for the retraction (GC refusal binding — open text is rejected). Adding a value is a Class-1 ISEDC matter.

reason.description: OPTIONAL human-readable free-text elaboration. The machine-actionable retraction class is carried by reason_class; this is operator context only and MUST NOT be parsed for decisions.

retracted_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp at which the retraction took effect.

retracted_by.description: OPTIONAL actor identity (operator email / service account) that authored the retraction, for audit-trail attribution.
